span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because each interneurone class terminates on a different pyramidal-cell compartment and each class fires at a different phase, the compartments of one pyramidal cell receive GABAergic input separated in time, which structures where and when that cell can integrate its inputs.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: During ripples the interneurones act not by shunting spikes but by delivering hyperpolarization timed to de-inactivate voltage-dependent ion channels, which then promotes the pyramidal cells' next discharge.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: O-LM cells go silent during ripples partly because their pyramidal input has a very low resting release probability that only repetitive presynaptic firing raises, and pyramidal cells emit only one or two spikes per ripple.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Bistratified cells firing at ripple frequency before the pyramidal cells could structure dendritic oscillations so that accumulating excitation triggers fast dendritic spikes that propagate to the soma.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: different interneurone types innervate different domains of the pyramidal cell, so the compartments receive GABAergic input differentiated in time rather than generalized inhibition
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: perisomatic cells fire before the pyramidal cells and can reset intrinsic membrane oscillations, which is how a single cell can synchronise thousands

span.label: and the same class fires differently in different brain states, so its target domain is modulated in a brain-state-dependent way

span.label: with the silence of one class during ripples not explicable by weak excitation alone, so an additional silencing mechanism must exist in the network

span.note: THE TWO CANNOT BE SEPARATED IN THIS STUDY - the DESIGN form of the negative relation (Q-286/Q-287). No edge type can express it: all eight assert that a relation HOLDS. A confounding statement bounds what the paper's own results can mean, and it lives where nothing downstream will find it. SCOPED TO A METHOD, which makes it the second case after marill1956 where the negative relation carries its own respect: 'WITHOUT ELECTRON MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION, in some cases, the cells cannot be distinguished'. span.note: RETRACTED: NO OPERATIONALISATION IS STATED ANYWHERE IN THIS SPAN. The edge is `domain --operationalised-as--> GABA`. Nothing here measures or defines a domain in terms of GABA, or GABA in terms of a domain; the passage speculates about WHY cortex needs so many interneuron types. Both endpoints are bare nouns lifted from a paragraph that uses them dozens of times in different roles - `domain` appears as 'domains of the pyramidal cell', 'the same domain', and 'the domain of integration', which are three different referents. THE PASSAGE'S OWN LAST SENTENCE IS 'Quotation withheld, but a temporal division of labour IS A POSSIBILITY.' The paragraph opens with a question, offers 'ONE CAN ARGUE THAT', rests its example on 'IS THOUGHT TO generate the action potential', and then raises its own counter-case. The author is not attributing, disputing or proposing a method - THE AUTHOR IS SAYING NOBODY KNOWS. An `operationalised-as` edge tells a reader this paper measured one thing as the other. A FOURTH MEMBER OF THE not-this-paper CLASS: speculative, and declared unresolved by its own author. Q-390. — strength of the relation: 1 — the argument for so many types: different domains have distinct roles and need independent modulation, with a temporal division of labour as the possibility
